title: Human-in-the-loop gates
summary: Which shell commands need a human: irreversible ones, outward-facing ones, project-specific patterns, and whether a host prompts natively or the pre-tool hook hands the command over.

questions.prompt: Which shell commands need a human?

options.label: Irreversible and outward-facing commands
options.tradeoff: Pushes, pull requests, releases and destructive commands always ask; more prompts, and a feature-branch push is not told from a default-branch push.

options.label: Irreversible commands only
options.tradeoff: Force-push, hard reset, rm -rf and destructive SQL ask; pushes and releases go through unprompted.

options.label: Outward-facing commands only
options.tradeoff: Pushes, pull requests, releases and publishing ask; local destructive commands go through unprompted.

options.label: Instruction only
options.tradeoff: No friction; depends on the agent complying.

questions.prompt: Which project commands also need a human? A command prefix or a /regex/.

decisions.title: Gated actions need a human
decisions.body:
## Decision

Irreversible and outward-facing shell commands need a human: native ask rules on hosts that support them, a pre-tool hook hand-over on the others (pack {{pack.id}}@{{pack.version}}).

## Why

Decision 0043 asks agents to stop before costly actions; nothing enforces it without a gate (decision 0094).

guardrails.title: Irreversible and outward-facing commands need a human

frontmatter.derivation-note: Given agents must hand over before irreversible or outward-facing actions (0043), the host must ask a human or deny the command, since an instruction alone fails silently.

enforcement.check: Host ask rules and the pre-tool hook gate these commands

guardrails.body:
## Guardrail

Shell commands of the irreversible and outward-facing classes need a human: do not run them yourself, ask the user to run them or approve them. Hosts with project ask rules prompt natively, because `go-getter apply` writes the rules into their settings. The other hosts get a hand-over: the pre-tool hook denies the command and the human runs it. `go-getter coverage` shows the tier per host. A mode that skips permission prompts defeats the native rules. A wrapped command (`sh -c`, `eval`) is matched on its literal text only.

decisions.title: Irreversible commands need a human
decisions.body:
## Decision

Irreversible shell commands (force-push, history rewrite, hard reset, `rm -rf`, destructive SQL, deleting a branch or tag) need a human: native ask rules on hosts that support them, a pre-tool hook hand-over on the others (pack {{pack.id}}@{{pack.version}}).

## Why

Decision 0043 asks agents to stop before costly actions; nothing enforces it without a gate (decision 0094).

decisions.title: Gated actions are advisory
decisions.body:
## Decision

Agents are told to hand over before irreversible or outward-facing actions; nothing blocks them (pack {{pack.id}}@{{pack.version}}).

## Why

The project accepted the risk for less friction (decision 0043).

guardrails.title: Agents hand over before irreversible or outward-facing actions

frontmatter.derivation-note: Given the project chose no mechanical gate, the rule rests on the agent following it.

guardrails.body:
## Guardrail

Ask the user before irreversible or outward-facing commands. Advisory (tier 1): nothing blocks them.
